facts.F100: Frontend. A Reports-owned component ReportNotes in pages/Common/Reports is rendered by ReportView beside ReportPanels, never inside ReportPanels or anything the print bundle imports, so print and PDF stay free of notes by construction; the print enforcement test gets a never-reaches rule. It is not extracted from DeliveryNotesPanel (FE2 will move that file); layout and copy are reused by value. Notes are read with a keyed TanStack query keyed by owner and report id, writes invalidate it. The add control shows when useMayEditReports(owner).isEditor; the change and delete controls show per note from canModify. The exact placement is decided at the UI sketch at the start of DELIVER.
facts.F101: Loading look and failure look of the notes area. Loading: the notes area is wrapped in WidgetBody with status from queryStatusOf, so it shows a lone spinner with the message Loading notes when it has nothing yet and dims the earlier list under a small spinner when it refetches; never an empty area that reads as no notes. Failure: WidgetBody shows the could-not-load message Could not load the notes with a retry, and the add control stays hidden while the list is unknown, so a note is never added blind. The report itself keeps its own status; a notes failure does not hide the numbers. A save in flight disables the Save control; a failed save keeps the typed text and shows the refusal under the field. The acceptance designer pins both states, and E2E waits for data-widget-status ready.
facts.F104: Cross-layer algebra. Domain (ReportNote, NoteSignature): states Unsigned(text, createdAt) and Signed(profileId, name, text, createdAt), optionally edited; operations Write, Revise, MayBeChangedBy; observations text, days, author name, canModify; equality by those observations. Application: ReportNoteCommands and ReportNoteQueries answer ReportOutcome Done, NotFound or Refused(code), never null for a domain outcome. Adapter: ReportRepository and the two controllers translate DbUpdateConcurrencyException to NotFound, outcomes to 200, 201, 204, 400, 403, 404, and the route guard refuses a caller without read or write access before any use case runs. Infrastructure: table ReportNotes with cascade to Reports and SetNull to UserProfiles; a failed save leaves prior notes intact.
facts.F105: Authority bounds carried: note text is plain text rendered as characters with line breaks kept; no markup is interpreted. Authority names no length bound; the design adds 2000 characters after trim as a labelled deviation. Authority names no bound on the number of notes; none is added. A text empty or only blanks is refused and nothing is saved (P4). The author name is the name when the note was written. The day shown is the instance-zone day of the instant. Newest first means ordered by CreatedAt then Id, both descending.

facts.F317: Placement. The note entity ReportNote sits in Models/Reports beside Report, not in Modules/Reports/Domain, because LighthouseAppContext (Data) must map it and the Reports rules R-RP2 and R-RP3 let only API, the composition root and Reports Application reach Domain. It is a kernel persistence carrier of the Report aggregate, moves with Report when S04b ratchets Models down, and adds one type to Models/Reports. Everything else is in Modules/Reports/Application: ports IReportNoteCommands, IReportNoteQueries and the driven port IReportNoteStore, use cases ReportNoteCommands and ReportNoteQueries, the caller choice type ReportNoteCaller (Anonymous, Signed, Unresolved) and the record ReportNoteRead. IReportNoteStore is implemented by the existing ReportRepository (one aggregate root, Report with its notes), so R-RP4 gains no outside type.
facts.F318: Maximum note length: 2000 characters after trimming, refused with code note-text-too-long. Reason: the live report lists every note without paging, so an unbounded text can swamp the report; 2000 holds a paragraph of context. Deviation from Delivery notes, which have none. The constant is ReportNote.LongestText; the mapping in LighthouseAppContext uses HasMaxLength(ReportNote.LongestText) on the text column, so the AddReportNotes migration creates the column bounded to 2000 and the database refuses a longer direct write. The number of notes per report is not capped (residue, owner maintainer).

Separate routes api/latest/teams/{teamId}/reports/{reportId}/notes and api/latest/portfolios/{portfolioId}/reports/{reportId}/notes (GET list newest first, POST, PUT {noteId}, DELETE {noteId}), two controllers over one ReportNotesControllerBase, mirroring TeamReportsController and PortfolioReportsController. ReportRead and the report routes the CLI and MCP clients read stay unchanged. The note DTO has id, text, createdAt, createdOn, lastEditedAt, lastEditedOn, authorDisplayName and canModify (decided on the server). A refusal is a ProblemDetails with a code: note-text-missing and note-text-too-long are 400, note-not-yours and note-author-unknown are 403.

facts.F322: Checker per claim. Quint 0.33.1 (model docs/feature/story-6564-report-notes/design/reportNoteModifyRule.qnt, receipt docs/feature/story-6564-report-notes/design/reportNoteModifyRule.receipt.txt) gives bounded checking of the safety law that a signed note is changed only by its signer over authentication switching on and off with two users and three note ids: a simulation of 2000 samples of 12 steps and a bounded verify of 8 steps found no violation, and a mutant that always answers true violates the invariant. That is bounded evidence, not a proof; the model does not generate a caller with authentication on and no profile, which is a separate rule pinned by native example tests (note-author-unknown). Cascade delete, the day reduction, ordering, the text rule and the print exclusion name no shared mutable protocol or crash window, so they get No model: single transition per request, state held by one database transaction, native example and property tests cover every transition. TLA+/TLC and Agda are not used: no liveness claim and no proof over types. Liveness has no claim: a note request is one synchronous transaction with no waiting step or background progress.

facts.F364: Author lookup through Access. Reports Application must not reach Access (R-RP5, R-A4), so the API adapter resolves the caller and hands Reports a value ReportNoteCaller, a choice of three: Anonymous (authentication off: the note is unsigned), Signed(profileId, displayName), Unresolved (authentication on but no profile resolves: no stable subject claim, or an API key with no profile row; or the authentication mode is not usable). The controller learns the mode from IAuthModeResolver.Resolve().Mode, the application's authentication mode (not the RBAC switch IRbacAdministrationService.IsRbacEnforcedAsync, which can be off while authentication is on, and never from a null profile). Mapping: Disabled gives Anonymous; Enabled gives Signed when ICurrentUserProfileService resolves a profile and Unresolved when it answers null; Misconfigured gives Unresolved, so a note is refused rather than saved unsigned when the mode is unsure; Blocked gives Unresolved as well, though BlockedModeFilter already answers 403 before any controller action runs on these routes. ReportNoteCommands refuses Add, Edit and Delete for Unresolved with code note-author-unknown (403), so an unsigned note exists only when authentication is off. Delivery notes keep their behaviour for this case (a pre-existing gap, reported to the maintainer, outside this Request). No edge from Reports to Access is added; the story 6382 contracts-only rule is unaffected because API is not a context and ReportNote has no navigation to UserProfile. The author name is the name at write time.

facts.F93: Aggregate and owners. A note is a child of the Report aggregate and is reached only through its owner and report id (a note reached through another report or owner finds nothing). Each decision has one owner: text normalisation, length bound, creation and revision sit on ReportNote (Write, Revise); who may change a note sits on the new kernel value NoteSignature, shared by ReportNote and DeliveryNote so the Delivery rule is decided once; refusals and ordering sit in ReportNoteCommands and ReportNoteQueries; write access on the owner stays a route guard (RbacGuard TeamWrite or PortfolioWrite), read access a TeamRead or PortfolioRead guard on the controller.
facts.F95: Concurrency: confirmed, the last save wins, as for Delivery notes. A note carries no concurrency token and a note change never touches the Report concurrency token, so adding or editing a note cannot conflict with an edit of the report. A change or delete of a note that another writer deleted meanwhile is translated in ReportRepository (DbUpdateConcurrencyException becomes a false save) into the port outcome NotFound, so no EF type reaches Application (R-RP5).
facts.F96: Deleting a Team or Portfolio: confirmed from the code. Reports carry cascade foreign keys to Teams and Portfolios (LighthouseAppContext ConfigureReports) and single and bulk report removal both end in IReportWriter.Remove plus one save (ReportCommands.Delete, ReportBulkRemover). ReportNotes gets a cascade foreign key to Reports, so notes follow in all three paths with no code of their own. The author foreign key to UserProfiles is SetNull, as for Delivery notes, so removing a person keeps the note and its captured name.
facts.F98: Time stays out of Application. ReportNoteCommands takes the instant as an argument and the read record carries instants; the controller holds ILighthouseClock, passes now and reduces CreatedAt and LastEditedAt to the instance-zone day in the DTO, as DeliveryNoteDto does. Reason: a clock in the new Application types would add listed edges to R-RP6, whose list may only shrink.
